blurb: MLB rules, records and ballparks from the 1880s to the pitch clock

questions.q: How many balls does it take for a batter to draw a walk?
questions.fact: In 1880 a walk took eight balls, and the modern count of four arrived in 1889.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Base on balls (1880 NL nine to eight; 1889 four)

questions.q: How far apart are the bases on a Major League Baseball diamond?
questions.fact: The pitching distance of 60 feet, 6 inches dates to 1893, when a rubber slab replaced the pitcher's box.
questions.src: Checked: textbook 90-ft bases; mlb.com, How baseball settled on 60 feet, 6 inches (1893, slab replaced box)

questions.q: In baseball scorekeeping, which position number is given to the shortstop?
questions.fact: That's why a double play that goes shortstop to second base to first is scored 6-4-3.
questions.src: Checked: textbook scorekeeping (6 = SS; 6-4-3 double play)

questions.q: When MLB's pitch clock debuted in 2023, how many seconds did a pitcher get with the bases empty?
questions.fact: With runners on base the limit was 20 seconds, and it was cut to 18 seconds in 2024.
questions.src: Checked: mlb.com glossary, Pitch Timer (2023: 15 empty / 20 runners; 2024: 18 with runners)

questions.q: MLB's yearly award for the best pitcher in each league is named after whom?
questions.fact: From 1956 to 1966, only one Cy Young Award was given each year, covering both leagues.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Cy Young Award (first 1956; one MLB-wide award through 1966; split 1967)

questions.q: Shohei Ohtani won the 2021 American League MVP award playing for which team?
questions.fact: The vote was unanimous: Ohtani received all 30 first-place votes.
questions.src: Checked: NBC LA, WTOP, CBS Sports, mlb.com headlines (Angels' Ohtani unanimous 2021 AL MVP)

questions.q: In 2016, the Chicago Cubs won their first World Series title since which year?
questions.fact: Game 7 against Cleveland went 10 innings, with a 17-minute rain delay before the 10th.
questions.src: Checked: WABE/NPR (first title since 1908); mlb.com, Game 7 delayed by rain entering 10th (17 min, after 9th)

questions.q: Joe DiMaggio's 56-game hitting streak and Ted Williams' .406 season both came in which year?
questions.fact: Williams entered the final day at .3995 but played a doubleheader anyway and went 6-for-8.
questions.src: Checked: baseballhall.org, Ted Williams goes 6-for-8 (.3995 entering final day, .406); DiMaggio streak 1941

questions.q: Which ballpark's towering left-field wall is nicknamed the Green Monster?
questions.fact: Ads covered the wall until 1947, when they came down and it was painted green.
questions.src: Checked: mlb.com Red Sox museum, Features of Fenway 1947 (ads removed, wall painted green)

questions.q: The outfield walls at Chicago's Wrigley Field are famously covered in what?
questions.fact: The ivy went up in September 1937, with bittersweet vines mixed in to help it fill in faster.
questions.src: Checked: mlb.com, Fact vs. Fiction: Origin of Wrigley's ivy (Sept 4, 1937; Boston ivy plus Japanese bittersweet)

questions.q: Chase Field, which opened in 1998 with a swimming pool beyond the outfield, was built for which team?
questions.fact: It was the first US stadium with a retractable roof over a natural grass field.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Chase Field (opened Mar 31, 1998 for Diamondbacks; pool right-center; first US retractable roof over natural grass)

questions.q: Willie Mays made his famous over-the-shoulder catch in the 1954 World Series at which ballpark?
questions.fact: He robbed Cleveland's Vic Wertz in Game 1, and the New York Giants went on to sweep the Series.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, 1954 World Series (Game 1 at Polo Grounds; Vic Wertz; Giants swept)

blurb: Stanley Cup lore, NHL legends and the rules of the rink

questions.q: In hockey, what is it called when one player scores three goals in a game?
questions.fact: It comes from cricket: in 1858, fans bought a hat for a bowler who took three wickets with three straight balls.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Hat-trick (H.H. Stephenson 1858, three wickets in three balls, hat from collection; in print 1865)

questions.q: A minor penalty in the NHL sends a player to the penalty box for how long?
questions.fact: After the 1955-56 season, the NHL let a power-play goal end a minor early, because Montreal kept scoring in bunches.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Penalty (ice hockey) (minor 2 min; rule changed after 1955-56 because of Montreal)

questions.q: Shooting the puck from your own half across the other team's goal line, untouched, is called what?
questions.fact: A team that is shorthanded because of a penalty is allowed to ice the puck.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Icing (ice hockey) (definition; waved off for shorthanded team)

questions.q: When the NHL returned from its 2004-05 lockout, what did it add to settle tied games?
questions.fact: Before then, regular-season games still tied after overtime simply ended in a tie.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Overtime (ice hockey) (shootout 2005-06; ties 1983-2004; 3-on-3 2015-16)

questions.q: Lord Stanley bought hockey's Stanley Cup in 1892 while serving as governor general of which country?
questions.fact: He paid 10 guineas for the silver bowl, about $48.67 at the time.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Stanley Cup (Governor General of Canada; bought 1892; 10 guineas = US$48.67)

questions.q: Which team won five straight Stanley Cups from 1956 to 1960?
questions.fact: Coach Toe Blake was behind the bench for all five of those championships.
questions.src: Checked: Hockey Hall of Fame, Montreal Canadiens 1955-56 to 1959-60 (Toe Blake coached all five)

questions.q: In 2018, which team won its first Stanley Cup by beating the Vegas Golden Knights in the Final?
questions.fact: Captain Alex Ovechkin won the Conn Smythe Trophy as the playoff MVP.
questions.src: Checked: CBS News, CBS Sports, Globe and Mail (Capitals' first Cup, Game 5 vs Vegas; Ovechkin Conn Smythe)

questions.q: When the Stanley Cup's bottom band fills up with names, what happens to its top band?
options: Melted down for a new band
Retired to the Hall of Fame
questions.fact: The other bands each move up a spot, and a new blank band is added at the bottom.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Stanley Cup (top band retired to HHOF vault; bands slide up; new blank band)

questions.q: Which hockey legend was nicknamed 'Mr. Hockey'?
questions.fact: He played pro hockey in six different decades, the last a single game in 1997 at age 69.
questions.src: Checked: history.com, Oct 3, 1997 (Howe, 69, one shift for Detroit Vipers; only pro in six decades)

questions.q: In 1988, Wayne Gretzky was traded from Edmonton to which team?
questions.fact: Edmonton got Jimmy Carson, Martin Gelinas, three first-round picks and $15 million.
questions.src: Checked: nhl.com, This date in NHL history: Aug. 9 (Carson, Gelinas, three 1st-rounders, $15 million)

questions.q: In 2015, Connor McDavid was drafted first overall by which team?
questions.fact: Edmonton won the draft lottery with 11.5% odds, landing its fourth No. 1 pick in six years.
questions.src: Checked: AP via abc7.com, Oilers win 2015 draft lottery (11.5% odds; No. 1 picks 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015)

questions.q: Who was the first NHL player to score 50 goals in a single season?
questions.fact: He scored No. 50 in the final game of the 1944-45 season, which was his 50th game.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, 50 goals in 50 games (Richard, Mar 18, 1945, 50th and final game; Geoffrion second)

blurb: World Cup glory, legendary clubs and the laws of the pitch

questions.q: How many players does each soccer team have on the field at once, including the goalkeeper?
questions.fact: Under the Laws of the Game, a match can't go on if a team is down to fewer than seven players.
questions.src: Checked: The FA, Laws of the Game Law 3 (max 11; may not start or continue with fewer than 7)

questions.q: Video assistant referees (VAR) were first used at a men's World Cup in which year?
questions.fact: Goal-line technology made its World Cup debut four years earlier, in Brazil.
questions.src: Checked: FourFourTwo, When was VAR first used at the World Cup (2018); Quartz (goal-line tech debut 2014 Brazil)

questions.q: Yellow and red cards were first used at the World Cup held in which year?
questions.fact: English referee Ken Aston came up with the idea while stopped at a London traffic light.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Ken Aston (Kensington High Street traffic light; cards first used 1970 World Cup)

questions.q: How far is the penalty mark from the goal line on a soccer field?
questions.fact: Irish linen manufacturer William McCrum proposed the penalty kick, and it entered the Laws of the Game in 1891.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, William McCrum (Irish linen manufacturer; proposed 1890, approved June 2, 1891; 12 yards)

questions.q: Which country hosted the 2010 World Cup, the first one held in Africa?
questions.fact: Spain won its first World Cup there, beating the Netherlands on Andres Iniesta's extra-time goal.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, 2010 FIFA World Cup final (Spain 1-0 aet, Iniesta 116', Spain's first title)

questions.q: Which country won the 1966 World Cup on home soil?
questions.fact: Geoff Hurst scored three times in the final, the first hat trick ever in a World Cup final.
questions.src: Checked: TSN, Mbappe second to score hat trick in World Cup final (Hurst first, 1966)

questions.q: Which country won the first FIFA Women's World Cup, held in China in 1991?
questions.fact: Michelle Akers scored both US goals in a 2-1 final win over Norway.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, 1991 FIFA Women's World Cup final (USA 2-1 Norway, Akers 20' and 78', Guangzhou)

questions.q: The original World Cup trophy, awarded from 1930 to 1970, was named after whom?
questions.fact: It was first called Victory and was renamed in 1946 in honor of Rimet, the FIFA president who launched the tournament.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, FIFA World Cup Trophy (first called Victory; renamed 1946 for Rimet; awarded 1930-1970)

questions.q: Lionel Messi played for which club from 2004 until his 2021 move to Paris Saint-Germain?
questions.fact: Barcelona's first promise to sign him, when he was 13, was famously written on a paper napkin.
questions.src: Checked: NPR/AP, Messi napkin contract (Dec 14, 2000, Carles Rexach, age 13)

questions.q: Which club went unbeaten through the 2003-04 Premier League season, earning the name 'The Invincibles'?
questions.fact: They won 26 and drew 12 of their 38 league matches.
questions.src: Checked: premierleague.com, 2003/04 Season Review: Invincible Arsenal (26W 12D 0L)

questions.q: Johan Cruyff and 'Total Football' led which Dutch club to three straight European Cups, 1971 to 1973?
questions.fact: Cruyff scored both goals in the 1972 final, a 2-0 win over Inter Milan.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, 1972 European Cup final (Ajax 2-0 Inter, Cruyff both goals); Ajax won 1971-73

questions.q: Manchester United signed a teenage Cristiano Ronaldo in 2003 from which club?
questions.fact: He won United over in a 2003 friendly played to open Sporting's new stadium.
questions.src: Checked: Planet Football (Aug 6, 2003 friendly opening Estadio Jose Alvalade; United signed him five days later)

blurb: Majors, Grand Slams and the legends of golf and tennis

questions.q: Which golf legend, nicknamed 'The Golden Bear,' won 18 major championships?
questions.fact: His last major came at the 1986 Masters, which he won at age 46.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Jack Nicklaus (Golden Bear; 18 majors; 1986 Masters at 46)

questions.q: In 2001, who became the first woman to shoot 59 in an LPGA event?
questions.fact: In 2003 she played the PGA Tour's Colonial, the first woman in a PGA Tour event since 1945.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, Annika Sorenstam (only woman to shoot 59 in competition, 2001 Standard Register PING; 2003 Colonial, first since Zaharias 1945)

questions.q: In 2021, who became the first Japanese man to win one of golf's major championships?
questions.fact: After his Masters win, caddie Shota Hayafuji put the pin back in the 18th hole, took off his cap and bowed to the course.
questions.src: Checked: AP via WITF and The Comeback (first Japanese man to win a men's major); Golf Channel (Hayafuji removed flag, replaced pin, bowed)

questions.q: Who became the first four-time winner of the Masters, in 1964?
questions.fact: Palmer won in 1958, 1960, 1962 and 1964, cheered on by fans known as Arnie's Army.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, 1964 Masters (first four-time winner); golfcompendium (1958, 1960, 1962, 1964)

questions.q: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on red clay?
questions.fact: Its stadium is named for Roland Garros, a French pilot who flew across the Mediterranean in 1913.
questions.src: Checked: textbook clay; thisdayinaviation.com, 23 September 1913 (Garros first to fly across the Mediterranean)

questions.q: In 2013, who became the first British man since Fred Perry in 1936 to win the Wimbledon singles title?
questions.fact: He beat Novak Djokovic in straight sets in the final.
questions.src: Checked: Wikipedia, 2013 Wimbledon men's singles (beat Djokovic 6-4 7-5 6-4; first Briton since Perry 1936)

questions.q: Who won tennis's first 'Golden Slam' in 1988: all four majors plus Olympic gold?
questions.fact: She beat Gabriela Sabatini in the Olympic final at the Seoul Games.
questions.src: Checked: olympics.com (IOC), Steffi Graf's 1988 Golden Slam (first ever; beat Sabatini 6-3 6-3 in Seoul)

questions.q: In 1969, which Australian won all four Grand Slam singles titles in the same calendar year?
questions.fact: He had also swept all four majors in 1962, as an amateur.
questions.src: Checked: Tennis Majors, Sept 9, 1969: Laver's second calendar Grand Slam (1962 as amateur)

questions.q: Which fruit, served with cream, is the classic snack at Wimbledon?
questions.fact: The first Wimbledon, in 1877, had only one event, men's singles; women's singles was added in 1884.
questions.src: Checked: textbook tradition; topendsports Wimbledon History (1877 gentlemen's singles only; ladies' singles 1884)

questions.q: In golf, what is a score of one under par on a single hole called?
questions.fact: Three under par on a hole is called an albatross, also known as a double eagle.
questions.src: Checked: textbook golf scoring terms (birdie -1, eagle -2, albatross/double eagle -3)

questions.q: In 1979, the team facing the US in golf's Ryder Cup expanded to take in players from where?
questions.fact: Spaniards Seve Ballesteros and Antonio Garrido were the first players from continental Europe to take part.
questions.src: Checked: golfcompendium, 1979 Ryder Cup (GB&I expanded to continental Europe; Ballesteros and Garrido first); Wikipedia, List of European Ryder Cup golfers (Irish players since 1953, 1973 a rename)

questions.q: In 2022, all four Grand Slams began using one rule for a final set tied at 6-6. What was it?
questions.fact: Before then, the French Open had no final-set tiebreak, and Wimbledon waited until 12-12.
questions.src: Checked: tennis.com, All Grand Slams to use 10-point tiebreaker at 6-6 (March 2022; prior rules per Slam)
